name: Saint Martin of the Tigers
text: Saint Martin of the Tigers (in Portuguese: São Martinho dos Tigres ), a settlement situated on a peninsula now known as the Tigres Island (in Portuguese: Ilha dos Tigres ), was originally a small but well-established fishing village. It was supplied with water from the nearby town of Foz do Cunene, at the mouth of the Cunene River . In the 1970s, Saint Martin of the Tigers was cut off from the mainland by the rising sea levels, and its water supply line was severed; both Tigres and Foz do Cunene were subsequently abandoned. The island, bound by the South Atlantic Ocean and the Tigres Strait , lies in a zone that is ideally suited for ecological projects. The island was mentioned in the BBC documentary "Unknown Africa: Angola".

name: Old Town
text: Old Town, Al-Ula , or al-Deera as it is locally called, is now all but a ghost town. It consists of a walled village of about 800 dwellings around the perimeter of the more ancient castle with narrow winding alleys, many of which are covered to shield the people from the heat of the sun. Most of the foundations of the buildings are stone, but the upper floors are made from mud bricks, while palm leaves and wood are used for the ceilings. Although many of these houses were probably rebuilt over time, their foundation is likely to be from the original construction of the town in the 13th century AD. 45 m (148 feet) above historic al-Ula, the town's Castle commands strategic views over the entire valley. It is sometimes referred to as the Castle of Musa bin Nusayr , the Umayyad -era army general who ruled over North Africa and was involved in conquering Andalusia in the early 8th century AD. He is said to have died in this castle on his way from Damascus to a pilgrimage in Mecca in 715 AD. Although the castle was rebuilt more than once during its long history, its origins date back to the 6th century BC. In fact, some of the foundation stones are from the original 2,600-year-old construction (according to signs posted). The castle is currently more of a bastion or watchtower once used to protect the town.

text: A few blocks of HDB flats (apartment flats) located in the Lim Chu Kang area of the island is known to be the only ghost town in Singapore. Named the Neo Tiew Estate (or officially the Lim Chu Kang Rural Centre ), it used to house residents before they were moved out of the vicinity in 2002 as part of an En-bloc scheme. Since then the Singapore government has declared it state land and nothing was done to demolish or renovate the flats. The area was used by the Singapore Army as a training facility from 2005 to 2009 until a newer training facility was built nearby in 2008. The facility was used most recently in 2012 when it was used to shoot scenes for the film Ah Boys to Men . As of today, its fate remains unknown.

name: Spinalonga
text: The island of Spinalonga is considered by some to be a ghost town. Serving as a leper colony for the first half of the 20th century, the island was abandoned when all its inhabitants were cured. By 1962 there were no permanent residents left. In recent years Spinalonga has become a tourist attraction as one of the last leper colonies to be closed down in Europe.

name: Old Perithia
text: Old Perithia (or Palea Perithia) is a ghost village on the northern side of Corfu on the slopes of Mount Pantokrator . The village was originally established in the 14th century, during Byzantine times due to the need of people to move from the coastal side and protect themselves from pirate and enemy attacks. Moreover, the diseases caused by mosquitoes on the coast drove residents to the mountain. When piracy was confronted from the Mediterranean Sea in the late 19th century, some inhabitants started to gradually move to the coasts where tourism had also started to develop.

The other three settlements were Óhuta (today Bükkszentlászló ), Újhuta (today Bükkszentkereszt ) and Répáshuta (which still exists). The last glass hut operated here until 1897; the village was still inhabited at the beginning of the 20th century. In its cemetery, the first burial was in 1843, and the last in 1926.

name: Roveraia
text: Roveraia, ghost village situated near Pratovalle, in the municipality of Loro Ciuffenna , in province of Arezzo , in Tuscany . The presence of the village is attested since the Middle Ages, when there was a tower. During World War II it was an important partisan base, reason why the village was destroyed by the German army. After the war the village was rebuilt. It was abandoned between the 1960s and the 1980s, when the last family who lived here left the village. Two projects have been proposed for the recovery of the village: in 2011 the proposal of Movimento Libero Perseo "Roveraia eco - lab", based on sustainability, and in 2019 there was a proposal aiming to recover the village with a mix of functions called "Ecomuseum of Pratomagno".

text: San Martino Monteneve in the province of Bolzano was a mining town at 2,355 m (7,726 feet) above sea level between the Ridanna Valley and the Passirio Valley. It sits atop of mining tunnels running from one valley to the other. It is now part of the Monteneve mining museum.

name: Schokland
text: Schokland , this was a very large island in the Middle Ages, but due to the rising sea level and major erosion from the Zuiderzee , the island became smaller and smaller. After a flood in 1825, life on the island was deemed too dangerous, and the two villages on the island: Emmeloord and Ens were abandoned. When the Noordoostpolder was created, Schokland became a landlocked elevation. The names Emmeloord and Ens were later used for villages in the newly created polder.

name: Pyramiden
text: Pyramiden ("The Pyramid") was a Russian settlement and coal mining community on the archipelago of Svalbard . It was founded by Sweden in 1910, and sold to the Soviet Union in 1927. The settlement, with a onetime population of 1,000 inhabitants, was abandoned in the late 1990s by its owner, the state-owned Soviet company Trust Artikugol, and is now a ghost town.

name: Czerwona Woda
text: Czerwona Woda ("Red Water") in Kłodzko Valley was established by German immigrants before WWII. Most of the abandoned houses are found in the mountains of Klodzko Valley.

name: Kłomino
text: Kłomino , near Borne Sulinowo in the northwest part of the country, was established as a place of residence for Soviet troops stationed in Poland with their families. The population was about 5,000. It was completely depopulated by 1992 after the collapse of the USSR. Only a few families live there now, but there are plans to repopulate the city.

name: Belchite
text: Belchite , in the province of Zaragoza , Aragon , is one of the best-known ghost towns in Spain. Before the 1930s, Belchite was a growing city, with many services. As a consequence of the Battle of Belchite , during the Spanish Civil War , the city was totally destroyed. Instead of a reconstruction, Franco decided to keep the ruins of the old town of Belchite intact as a memorial of the battle. As of 1964, the town was totally deserted, the inhabitants having been removed to Belchite Nuevo, on the side of the old town. The ruins, which are not accommodated for tourism, are visited by more than 10,000 tourists annually. It is also a well-known meeting point for Francoist nostalgics, especially Falangists .

name: Birchinlee
text: Birchinlee in Derbyshire was a village built by the Derwent Valley Water Board for the workers (and their families) who constructed the Derwent and Howden Dams between 1902 and 1916.

name: Derwent
text: Derwent in Derbyshire was demolished in the 1940s to make way for the Ladybower Reservoir .

name: Cuddington
text: Cuddington was a hamlet in Surrey that was demolished in the sixteenth century so that Nonsuch Palace (itself later demolished) could be built.

name: Dunwich
text: Dunwich , a once-thriving town on the Suffolk coast, began to decline in 1286 when a storm swept much of it into the sea. Subsequent storms and coastal erosion have since claimed all but a few of the remaining buildings.

name: Ewden Village
text: Ewden Village in the Civil Parish of Stocksbridge was a timber-built village, completed in 1929 to house workers working on the Morehall and Broomhead reservoirs.

name: Hallsands
text: Hallsands is a coastal village in Devon that was destroyed by a storm in 1917.

name: Hambleton
text: Hambleton , in Rutland , is a civil parish that once included the settlements of Middle Hambleton and Nether Hambleton, which were both flooded in 1975 to create Rutland Water .

name: Heathrow
text: Heathrow , a small village in Middlesex , was demolished in 1944 so that Heathrow Airport could be built.

name: Mardale
text: Mardale Green in the Lake District was demolished and flooded in 1935 to create Haweswater Reservoir .

name: Martinsthorpe
text: Martinsthorpe , in Rutland , is one of the few civil parishes in England to have a population of zero.

name: Ravenser Odd
text: Ravenser Odd is a village on the coast of the East Riding of Yorkshire , that was swept away in the Grote Mandrenke storm of 1362.

name: Ravenspurn
text: Ravenspurn , also on the coast of the East Riding of Yorkshire, south of Ravenser Odd, and near Spurn Head , was abandoned in the 19th century and was swept into the North Sea .

name: the Isles of Scilly that
text: Samson is a remote island of the Isles of Scilly that has been deserted since 1855.

name: Shipden
text: Shipden , in Norfolk , was washed into the sea in the 14th century.

name: Stanlow Island
text: Stanlow Island , in Merseyside found on the Manchester Ship Canal was abandoned in the 1990s due to hazards of living nearby a refinery .

name: Tide Mills
text: Tide Mills in East Sussex was condemned as unfit for habitation and abandoned in 1939.

name: Wyck
text: Wyck , a deserted medieval village in West Tisbury, abandoned in the 14th century.

name: Wharram Percy
text: Wharram Percy is a medieval village in North Yorkshire abandoned in the early 16th century for more sheep pasture.

name: In 1942 and 1943
text: In 1942 and 1943, in preparation for the Allied assault on Normandy, several villages were evacuated to be used as training grounds for the British Army and U.S. forces. This was intended to be a temporary arrangement, but many of the villages remained abandoned, and are used for military training to this day. Some of these villages are listed below; most of them are located within the Stanford Battle Area in Norfolk.

name: Boreraig
text: Boreraig , on the Isle of Skye , was one of many villages that were forcibly evacuated by Scottish aristocrats in the 18th and 19th centuries.

name: Bothwellhaugh
text: Bothwellhaugh , in North Lanarkshire , is a former coal mining town that now lies under Strathclyde Loch .

name: Hallaig
text: Hallaig , on the island of Raasay , depopulated as part of the Highland Clearances and subject of a famous Gaelic poem by Sorley MacLean .

name: Mingulay
text: Mingulay , an island at the southern end of the Outer Hebrides , depopulated as part of the ongoing effects of the Highland Clearances, the village on the island finally abandoned in 1912.

name: The Monach Islands
text: The Monach Islands , also known as Heisker, in the Outer Hebrides; the village abandoned in 1932 and depopulated in 1942 with the closure of the lighthouse.

name: North Rona
text: North Rona is a remote Scottish island that has been deserted since 1844.

name: Scarp
text: Scarp , whose last permanent inhabitants left for nearby Harris in 1971. Site of Gerhard Zucker 's experiments with rocket mail .

name: Saint Kilda
text: Saint Kilda is an archipelago in the Outer Hebrides that was abandoned in 1930, and is now a World Heritage Site .

name: Capel Celyn
text: Capel Celyn in Gwynedd was flooded in 1965 to create the reservoir Llyn Celyn .

name: Llangaffo
text: Llangaffo in Anglesey , north of Dwyran , south of Gaerwen and northwest of Llanidan where the school had closed down and maintained its ghost town status until 2023.

name: Nant Gwrtheyrn
text: Nant Gwrtheyrn in Gwynedd is a former quarry town that became abandoned during World War II, but is now the site of a Welsh language learning centre.

name: Cinchona
text: Cinchona (Sarapiquí, Alajuela ) was destroyed by the 2009 Costa Rica earthquake , which left 25 people dead and five missing.

name: Petite Savanne
text: Petite Savanne was destroyed when Tropical Storm Erika unleashed a series of deadly mudslides in 2015; the government ordered a mandatory and permanent evacuation of all residents.

name: San Miguel Los Lotes
text: San Miguel Los Lotes was buried by a pyroclastic flow during the 2018 Volcán de Fuego eruption on 3 June 2018.

name: San Juan Parangaricutiro
text: San Juan Parangaricutiro is a village in Michoacán that was buried by ash and lava in 1943, during the formative eruption of Parícutin .

name: Ojuela
text: Ojuela , a mining town near Durango City , was abandoned when the area's ore supply was exhausted.

name: Real de Catorce
text: Real de Catorce was once a flourishing silver mining town in northern Mexico. Its dramatic landscapes and buildings have been used by Hollywood for movies such as The Mexican (2001) with Brad Pitt and Julia Roberts . Recent efforts to adapt the town to tourism have created a mixture of ghost town and heritage tourist site adapted to visitors in search of interesting history in the country.

name: San Antonio de la Iguana
text: San Antonio de la Iguana, Nuevo León

name: Thompson's Landing
text: Thompson's Landing was a port at the mouth of the Colorado River . During the early settlement of Arizona, shallow-draft steamboats plied the lower reaches of the river.

name: Jalapa del Marqués
text: Jalapa del Marqués , Oaxaca was an important town under precolonial times and after the Spanish conquest. It was flooded in 1961 in order to make way for a dam. The town was relocated south. Only the former Dominican convent remains.

name: Santo Tomás de los Plátanos
text: Santo Tomás de los Plátanos , Mexico was a small town in the former frontier between the Purépecha Empire and the Aztec Empire , but was flooded in 1956 in order to make way for a dam. A solemn procession with the church's icons was made to the new location, uphill. Only the belltower of the church remains.

name: Padilla
text: Padilla, Tamaulipas was stablished in 1749 by José de Escandón , served as capital of Tamaulipas between 1824 and 1825, was the place where Agustín de Iturbide was executed and Manuel Mier y Terán took his life. However, the town was flooded in 1971 to make way to a dam, and was relocated upstream. Only ruins remain from the original town, among them the church, the school and the monument marking the place of Iturbide's execution.

name: Ciudad Guerrero
text: Ciudad Guerrero , Tamaulipas was stablished in 1749 by José de Escandón, served as capital of the Republic of the Rio Grande in 1840. It was abandoned in 1953 in order to make way for the Falcón Dam . When the waters recede, most of the town's stone houses and church are visitable and in decent conditions.

name: Santiago Tlaltepoxco
text: Santiago Tlaltepoxco, Hidalgo . The town was cleared since the 19th century in order to make way to the railroad from Mexico to Paso del Norte . Only a very ruined church and an old bridge from the old royal road remains.

name: Chupícuaro
text: Chupícuaro , Guanajuato was one of the oldest settlements in the northern limits of Mesoamerica , where several ancient objects have been found defined as of a particular culture, identified by its name. However, it was flooded in 1949 in order to make way for a dam, and its inhabitants relocated north to a new settlement called Nuevo Chupícuaro . Some intensive excavations were done to salvage as much prehispanic artifacts as possible before the flood took over. It's been almost always covered by water ever since, and the ruined remains of the church rarely surface. In 2013, after a prolongated drought that lowered the lake's levels, the municipality was able to recover the top piece of the belltower, which was installed in the atrium of the new town's church.

name: San Luis Taxhimay
text: San Luis Taxhimay, Mexico , also known as San Luis de las Peras , was a town in the municipality of Villa del Carbón . It was flooded in 1934 in order to make way for a dam. Only the belltower of the main church and the façade of a chapel remain.

name: San Francisco Bojay
text: San Francisco Bojay, Hidalgo was a town in the municipality of Tula flooded in 1949 in order to make way for the Endhó dam. The suburbs were cut in two, becoming separate villages, while its church remained in the middle, often flooded but with its belltower still standing.

name: San Antonio Corrales
text: San Antonio Corrales, Hidalgo was a town in the municipality of Alfajayucan flooded in 1950 in order to make way to a dam. The town was relocated to the south, while the small church complex, only remaining building in the original location, has an excellent conservation status.

name: La Pupa
text: La Pupa, Nayarit was a mining town that rose around an old hacienda . With the mine's closure, the town was progressively abandoned. The ruins are still in relatively good condition.

name: El Triunfo
text: El Triunfo, Baja California Sur was stablished as a mining town in the late 18th century, was mostly abandoned in 1926 after the mines were shut. Not entirely deserted, it is however barely inhabited. Some buildings have since been restored in order to house touristic facilities.

name: San Antonio
text: San Antonio, Baja California Sur was stablished as a mining town in the late 18th century, and became capital of the territory of Baja California in 1829, losing a while later that privilege to La Paz . It was mostly abandoned in 20th century after the mines were shut. Not entirely deserted, it is however barely inhabitted.

name: Cerro de San Pedro
text: Cerro de San Pedro , San Luis Potosí is a depopulated mining town. During the 20th century a sour work relationship between the mine operators and the workers closed the mine in 1948, causing its almost total depopulation. The mineral hasn't been drained, but the operation of an open pit mine started in 1998. The pit is directly behind the town. This and the disappearance of the namesake hill ( Cerro de San Pedro means "St. Peter's Hill") has threatened the townsite, considered an area of colonial monuments.

name: San Pedro de los Pozos
text: San Pedro de los Pozos, Guanajuato . Not completely abandoned yet and with a second life oriented to tourism, it was a mining town that was abandoned when the mines flooded.

name: Bolaños
text: Bolaños , Jalisco . Former important mining town, it has been reduced to being barely more than a village with less than 1000 inhabitants. Its ruins (the main church, the mint, palaces, etc.) still persist as the reminder of a time past.

name: La Encarnación
text: La Encarnación, Hidalgo.

name: El Rosario
text: El Rosario, Baja California Sur.

name: Misnébalam
text: Misnébalam, Yucatán

name: Amersham
text: Amersham in the Saint Anthony Parish was abandoned in the wake of the Soufrière Hills eruption in 1997.

name: Plymouth
text: Plymouth was once the seat of government in Montserrat, and home to around 4,000 people, until it was almost completely destroyed by the Soufrière Hills volcano in 1997. The entire southern half of the island is now off-limits, leaving over 30 villages and towns abandoned.

name: L'Île-aux-Marins
text: L'Île-aux-Marins ("Sailor's Island") is a ghost town/island located a few miles away from the island of Saint-Pierre. Once inhabited by over 600 fishermen, families and tradesmen, the island was progressively abandoned until the last inhabitant left in 1965. The island is now a tourist attraction.

name: Old Adaminaby drowned by new lake of Snowy Mountains Hydro-E
text: Old Adaminaby drowned by new lake of Snowy Mountains Hydro-Electric scheme. Town relocated.

name: Ballara
text: Ballara is an abandoned copper mining town in Queensland .

name: Betoota
text: Betoota , in Queensland , is the smallest designated town in Australia; its last permanent resident died in 2004.

name: Big Bell
text: Big Bell is a former mining town in Western Australia .

name: Boydtown
text: Boydtown , in New South Wales , was originally settled and then abandoned in the 1840s. It remained abandoned until the 1930s. It is now a growing town with commercial and residential developments.

name: Broad Arrow
text: Broad Arrow was a gold rush town in Western Australia that had been abandoned by the 1920s.

name: Calcifer
text: Calcifer was a mining town established on the Atherton Tablelands in 1894, abandoned by 1907.

name: Cassilis
text: Cassilis was a gold rush town in Victoria that declined during the First World War.

name: Collingwood
text: Collingwood in Queensland was established in 1878, but abandoned about 1900 when it was outcompeted as a regional centre by nearby Winton . There is a commemorative marker at the old graveyard listing eight persons known to be buried there.

name: Cook
text: Cook is an isolated town in South Australia built around a railway station, which was closed down in 1997.

name: Copperfield
text: Copperfield is a former copper mining town in Queensland .

name: Cossack
text: Cossack in Western Australia was a flourishing port town in the 1800s, and profited greatly from the pearling industry. It began to decline during the 20th century.

name: Crotty
text: Crotty in Western Tasmania was abandoned when the nearby mine closed down. It is now submerged beneath Lake Burbury .

name: Cudgegong
text: Cudgegong was a small town in central western New South Wales. Windamere dam now exists where the town once stood, but ruins can be seen in times of drought when the dam dries up.

name: Denison Town
text: Denison Town in New South Wales.

name: Farina
text: Farina in South Australia was abandoned when its settlers found that the climate was unsuitable for arable farming.

name: Glen Davis
text: Glen Davis in New South Wales was the centre of an oil shale industry during the Second World War; the mine was closed down in 1952.

name: Goldsworthy
text: Goldsworthy is a former iron ore mining town in Western Australia .

name: Gwalia
text: Gwalia in Western Australia was abandoned when its gold mine closed down in 1963.

name: Hill End
text: Hill End in New South Wales was never fully abandoned and is now a popular tourist town.

name: Iron Baron
text: Iron Baron is a former mining town in South Australia .

name: Jay Creek
text: Jay Creek in the Northern Territory was a government settlement for Indigenous Australians in the 1920s and 30s.

name: Joadja
text: Joadja is a former mining town in New South Wales that had become abandoned by 1911.

name: Kanowna
text: Kanowna is a town in Western Australia that flourished during a gold rush in the late 19th century, and declined during the Great Depression .

name: Kiandra
text: Kiandra is a former gold mining town in New South Wales .

name: Linda
text: Linda is a former mining town in Tasmania .

name: Malcolm
text: Malcolm is a former gold mining town in Western Australia .

name: Mary Kathleen
text: Mary Kathleen is a former mining town in Queensland that was deserted after the mine closed down in 1982.

name: Maytown
text: Maytown is a former mining town in the Palmer River goldfields of Queensland .

name: Moliagul
text: Moliagul is a former gold mining town in Victoria ; it was here that the world's largest gold nugget, known as the " Welcome Stranger ", was discovered in 1869.

name: Mount Britton
text: Mount Britton is a former gold mining town in Queensland .

name: Mount Cuthbert
text: Mount Cuthbert is a former copper mining town in Queensland .

name: Mount Mulligan
text: Mount Mulligan is a former coal mining town in Queensland that closed down in 1957.

name: Nannine
text: Nannine is a former gold mining town in Western Australia .

name: Newnes
text: Newnes is a former oil shale mining site in New South Wales .

name: Old Tallangatta
text: Old Tallangatta , in Victoria , was abandoned when most of the township was moved 8 km (5 miles) west due to the enlargement of Lake Hume . The current township of Tallangatta has approximately 1,000 residents.

name: Ophir
text: Ophir is a former gold mining town in New South Wales .

name: Ora Banda
text: Ora Banda is a former gold mining town in Western Australia .

name: Paradise
text: Paradise is a former gold mining town in Queensland .

name: Whilst not a town
text: Whilst not a town, Parramatta Road in Sydney has over 100 abandoned and boarded-up stores on its 23-kilometre-long (14 mi) strip. The most affected suburbs on the road are Concord and Leichhardt , which would feature empty and derelict shops here and there.

name: Pillinger
text: Pillinger was a port town established in Tasmania to ship ore from the nearby mines.

name: Ravenswood
text: Ravenswood in north-eastern Queensland was a ghost town for many years, due to the declining gold rushes, but new gold discoveries in the area and improved mineral processing technologies have boosted the economy of the area and revived the town.

name: Selwyn
text: Selwyn in the Shire of Cloncurry, Queensland , is a former copper mining town.

name: Shay Gap
text: Shay Gap in Western Australia 's Pilbara region was a company town that existed for roughly 20 years until the iron ore mining ceased in 1993.

name: Silverton
text: Silverton is a former silver mining town in New South Wales that was deserted when more lucrative silver-lead-zinc ore was discovered at nearby Broken Hill .

name: Tarcoon
text: Tarcoon, New South Wales

name: Walhalla
text: Walhalla, Victoria , was never fully abandoned and has now become a popular tourist town.

name: Western Tyers
text: Western Tyers , a timber community in Victoria , was abandoned after the timber mill closed in 1969.

name: Whroo
text: Whroo , a former mining town in Victoria .

name: Wittenoom
text: Wittenoom in Western Australia was the country's only source of blue asbestos ( crocidolite ) in the 1950s and 60s. The mine was shut down in 1966, and the residents of the town were gradually relocated, due to concerns that the asbestos in the air posed a danger to their health.

name: Yerranderie
text: Yerranderie is a former silver mine in New South Wales .

name: Banaba
text: Banaba , which once had a phosphate mining town.

name: Paris
text: Paris

name: Tebunginako
text: Tebunginako , where most of the town has been flooded by rising sea levels .

name: Denniston
text: Denniston was a coal mining town in the West Coast Region of the South Island of New Zealand. Formerly with a population of around 1400, it now has about ten residents.

name: Hardwicke
text: Hardwicke was the sole European settlement in the Auckland Islands , founded in 1849 but abandoned in 1851.

name: Jamestown
text: Jamestown was a settlement in what is now Fiordland National Park .

name: Kelso
text: Kelso was abandoned after severe and repeated flooding in the late 1970s and early 1980s.

name: Lyell
text: Lyell was a gold mining town in the Buller Gorge in the South Island.

name: Macetown
text: Macetown was a gold rush town in Central Otago that started to decline during the 20th century.

name: Nenthorn
text: Nenthorn was an Otago gold mining town from 1888 until the 1890s, abandoned when its mining efforts collapsed. Only two ruined buildings and the remains of a battery remain.

name: Port Craig
text: Port Craig is a former logging township on the southwest coast of the South Island.

name: Port Molyneux
text: Port Molyneux was a port at the mouth of the Clutha River in Otago . After a flood caused the river mouth to move, the town was abandoned.

name: Port Pegasus
text: Port Pegasus was a township on the south coast of Stewart Island in southern New Zealand.

name: Rotowaro
text: Rotowaro , a coal mining town, was removed in the 1980s to make way for an opencast mine. It is the site of the now abandoned Rotowaro Carbonisation Plant .

name: Te Hutewai
text: Te Hutewai was a very small farming community located around 10 km south of Raglan , in the Waikato District . A school was built but was burnt down in the 1960s and the area today is now farmland.

name: Te Wairoa
text: Te Wairoa , also called "The Buried Village", was a small Māori village that was destroyed by the 1886 eruption of Mount Tarawera .

name: Venture
text: Venture, a small beech bark processing settlement in the Awaroa Inlet of the Abel Tasman National Park , was abandoned as the value of the bark declined and the cost of transport increased into the remote area. The remains of the foundations of the school house and assorted buildings remain in the bush today, although fire, time and the encroachment of the bush has rendered the ruins little more than a collection of stones and bricks. The settlement can only be reached by walking up a rarely used and poorly maintained track at low tide. The settlement and track are on the estate administered by the Department of Conservation .

name: Waiuta
text: Waiuta was a gold mining town in the West Coast Region of the South Island of New Zealand until 1951.

name: Villa Epecuén
text: The small lakeside resort town of Villa Epecuén was abandoned on 10 November 1985, after a series of heavy rains caused the lake water levels to rise and flood the town. The remains of the town re-emerged on 11 May 2013, when the waters of the lake receded.

name: Caraíbas
text: The small village of Caraíbas, in the municipality of Itacarambi , suffered a rare earthquake in the early morning of 9 December 2007. It measured 4.9 on the Richter scale . Located over a geological fault , the village of 76 families was evacuated and has been abandoned ever since.

name: Fordlândia
text: Fordlândia was established by American industrialist Henry Ford in 1928 near Santarém . This was done to mass-produce natural rubber . Built in inadequate terrain, designed with no knowledge of tropical agriculture, and managed with little regard for local culture, the enterprise was an absolute failure; in 1934, the Ford factory was relocated to Belterra , but ultimately closed down in 1945.

name: Velho Airão
text: Velho Airão (formerly Airão) was founded in 1694 in the modern state of Amazonas . It gained relevance as a collection and distribution point for natural rubber in the Negro , Jaú and Branco Rivers but went bankrupt in the early 20th century, when the United Kingdom started purchasing rubber from British Malaya . This resulted in its inhabitants abandoning the town, most relocating to Itapeaçu, which was renamed to Novo Airão . After the last resident left in 1985, the site was utilized by the Brazilian Navy for firing practice until it was declared a protected historical landmark by the IPHAN in 2005.

name: Chaitén
text: Chaitén is a small city in southern Chile that was heavily damaged by a volcanic eruption.

name: Humberstone and Santa Laura Saltpeter Works
linked_article: Humberstone and Santa Laura Saltpeter Works
text: Humberstone and Santa Laura Saltpeter Works are two former saltpeter refineries that have been declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site .

name: La Noria
text: La Noria, a deserted mining town in the Atacama Desert . The infamous Atacama skeleton was found at La Noria.

name: Port Famine
text: Port Famine ( Spanish : Puerto Hambre ) is possibly Chile's oldest ghost town. It was founded in the Strait of Magellan in 1584 by Pedro Sarmiento de Gamboa . Starvation and the cold climate killed all of the inhabitants. The English navigator Sir Thomas Cavendish landed at the site in 1587. He found only ruins of the settlement, and renamed the place "Port Famine".

name: Sewell
text: Sewell is a former mining town that was once home to at least 14,000 people.

name: Armero
text: Armero was left in ruins by a volcanic eruption in 1985 that killed over 20,000 inhabitants. Survivors of the tragedy left for other towns, and Armero is currently unpopulated.

name: Bojayá
text: Bojayá is a small town in the Chocó department, that was attacked by the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) on 2 May 2002. Most of the inhabitants hid in the church; A FARC mortar bomb landed in the building, killing approximately 140 people, including 40 children. Today, Bojayá is a ghost town and though plans have been made to rebuild it, it will not be on the exact location of the massacre .

name: Gramalote
text: Gramalote , a town in Norte de Santander Department , was abandoned due to massive mudslides brought by flooding near the area.

name: San Cayetano
text: San Cayetano was permanently evacuated in 1999 as a result of a geological fault. Rebuilt in 2002 in a new location.

name: Sativanorte
text: Sativanorte was abandoned in 1933 after the land sinking. The population was rebuilt in a new location the following year.

name: Siberia
text: Siberia (Colombia) [ es ] , a town in Cundinamarca , was abandoned in 1998.

name: Guasabra [ es ] district of Santa Fe de Antioquia
text: Guasabra [ es ] district of Santa Fe de Antioquia had to be abandoned due to geological instability, it was later rebuilt near its original location.

name: San José de Maipures [ es ]
text: San José de Maipures [ es ] was a small town in the department of Vichada , it was the first capital of the department.

name: Santa María la Antigua del Darién
linked_article: Santa María la Antigua del Darién
text: Santa María la Antigua del Darién , initially founded by Spanish conquistadors, but was abandoned later.

name: Guisanbourg
text: Guisanbourg was the former administrative centre of what is now Régina . The discovery of gold in 1855, led to its demise, and in the mid-1980s, the last citizen left the town.

name: Ituni
text: Ituni , a former bauxite mining town in decline since the mines closed.

name: Jonestown
text: Jonestown was established in the 1970s by members of the Peoples Temple , led by Jim Jones . On 18 November 1978, Jones orchestrated a mass suicide, resulting in the death of 913 of Jonestown's 1,110 inhabitants. The town now stands in ruins, and is being slowly reclaimed by the jungle.

name: Machu Picchu
text: Machu Picchu was built during the Inca Empire and is now a popular tourist site.

name: Potosí
text: Potosí was a Venezuelan town in the western state of Táchira. The town was deliberately flooded by the Venezuelan government in 1985 to build a hydroelectric dam. In 2010, the town was uncovered for the first time since its flooding due to a drought caused by the weather phenomenon called El Niño .
